correctness.rationale: Marco Fava arXiv:2610.01829v1 Theorem 1.1 explicitly supplies Tate-type Hodge–Euler polynomial for the smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack Jbar_(2,1): L^6+5L^5+15L^4+20L^3+15L^2+5L+1, so odd cohomology vanishes and the reduced even Betti polynomial is B(t)=1+5t+15t^2+20t^3+15t^4+5t^5+t^6. Modulo 3 it is t^6+2t^5+2t^3+2t+1. The submitted exact checker establishes gcd(B,t^(3^2)-t)=1, gcd(B,t^(3^3)-t)=1 and t^(3^6)=t mod B (Rabin degree-six irreducibility criterion); an independent SymPy irreducibility calculation confirmed irreducibility over F3. Gauss implies Z-irreducibility. If X had the Q-cohomology of a product of connected smooth proper positive-dimensional complex Deligne–Mumford stacks, Kunneth P_X(s)=P_Y(s)P_Z(s) and nonnegative Betti coefficients plus vanishing odd cohomology of X force P_Y,P_Z even-only with b0=1. Positive dimension and top cohomology make both reduced even polynomials nonconstant, contradicting B irreducible. This only rules out actual products or the asserted rational cohomology tensor products, not fibrations, birational maps or motivic splitting.

value.rationale: The compactified universal genus-two Jacobian is a natural moduli stack; its newly calculated rational cohomology detects a geometrically relevant global obstruction to decomposing it into positive-dimensional proper factors. Although the irreducibility computation is elementary and the Betti vector is prior knowledge, the exact cohomological indecomposability is a motivated structural statement and independent application, not merely a re-tabulation of Betti numbers. The narrow rational/topological scope is essential.
